attributes.body_ja:
「逆（ぎゃく）に」は何（なに）かが前（まえ）に述（の）べられたことと「反対（はんたい）」であることを表（あらわ）します。これは名詞（めいし）の「逆（ぎゃく）」に助詞（じょし）の「に」が付（つ）いたもので、副詞（ふくし）として機能（きのう）します。たいていは「(A) とは反対（はんたい）に (B)」という意味（いみ）で二（ふた）つの節（せつ）を繋（つな）ぐ形（かたち）で使（つか）われます。

現代（げんだい）の砕（くだ）けた会話（かいわ）では、話（はなし）の流（なが）れを変（か）えて質問（しつもん）し返（かえ）すときに「逆（ぎゃく）に」を文（ぶん）の頭（あたま）で使（つか）うことがあります。また、相手（あいて）の発言（はつげん）に同意（どうい）できないときや、それを受（う）け止（と）めた上（うえ）で自分（じぶん）の意見（いけん）を返（かえ）すときに「むしろ」「それより」「一方（いっぽう）で」のようなニュアンスでスラング的（てき）に使（つか）われることもあります。
attributes.body:
逆（ぎゃく）に is a grammar pattern that indicates that something is 'contrary' to what has previously been said. This is a structure made up of the noun 逆（ぎゃく） 'reverse', 'opposite', or 'converse', and に. Due to the inclusion of に, this phrase behaves adverbially, and will usually appear between two phrases, to indicate that 'on the contrary to (A), (B)', or 'conversely to (A), (B)'.

In modern Japanese, 逆（ぎゃく）に is also frequently used at the beginning of a sentence, simply to indicate a rebuttal toward something that someone has just said, or as a slang version of 別（べつ）に when asked questions about preferences, or similar things.

逆に is colloquial, meaning on the contrary or contrary to expectations, often introducing a reversal, as in 応援したのに逆に怒られた (I cheered them on, but on the contrary, they got angry). に反して means contrary to or against, used with rules, intentions, or expectations, as in 規則に反して行動した (He acted against the rules). 逆に can stand alone, while に反して must follow something.

むしろ and 逆に both express contrast, but with different nuances. むしろ presents a preference or clarification, e.g. 話すよりむしろ相手の話を聞きたい ('I'd rather listen than talk'). 逆に highlights an outcome opposite to what was expected, e.g. 喜んでくれると思ったが逆に怒られた ('I thought they'd be happy, but they got mad instead').

却って and 逆に both express something being counter to expectations, like the English 'on the contrary'. 却って is more formal, and occurs primarily in writing in the context of a full sentence or explanation. In contrast, 逆に is quite casual, and can be used in the same way as 却って, but also as an interjection at the beginning of a sentence or phrase, e.g. 逆にたかし君はどう思いますか？ ('On the contrary, what do you think, Takashi?').
